title: We Come, O Lord, Before Thy Throne
description: We Come, O Lord, Before Thy Throne in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 835 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Seamen”, where the book credits them to the Select Hymns.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We come, O Lord, be-fore thy throne, And, with u-ni-ted pleas, We meet and pray for those who roam Far off up-on the seas.

lines: We come, O Lord, before thy throne,
We meet and pray for those who roam
O, may the Holy Spirit bow
Till tears of deep repentance flow
Then may a Saviour's dying love
And waft him to the port above

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
